title: Integration Resilience Microdeck for SE + Ops
content:
Purpose and audience:
A compact, slide-style sales enablement microdeck for SEs and Ops to use during initial integration calls and pilot runbooks. Focus is on practical scripts and checklists to handle latency/regression concerns, fallback paths, and canary rollback heuristics. Not customer-facing as-is — intended for quick coach/coach-with-customer scenarios.

One-line pitch (for SEs):
'How we keep your app online with predictable latency and safe fallbacks while you tune quality — checklist, scripts, and rollback play in one slide deck.'

What this microdeck contains (slides outline):
1) 20s opener: expected behavior + sweet spot use cases
   - Quick phrase: "Predictable inference, built-in fallbacks, transparent economics."
   - Use cases to call out: chat assistants (low-latency requirements), classified document processing (throughput bursts), embeddings batch jobs (cost sensitivity).

2) Golden flow (diagram placeholder)
   - Request arrives -> Smart router -> Primary model variant (low-latency) -> KV/prefix cache hit? -> Response
   - On degradation: automated fallback to cost-optimized or smaller model variant -> degraded-quality badge + telemetry alert -> ops notification
   - Slide note: add runtime diagram from engineering (TODO: embed svg from platform repo)

3) Pilot checklist (things to do on day 0–7)
   - Define 3 workload profiles (p50 prompt len, p95 prompt len, batch size)
   - Set latency SLO target and acceptable quality delta (example: p95 < 450ms, quality drop <= 5% on eval prompts)
   - Configure routing policy: prefer region X, fallback to variant Y, max-allowed-queue-ms = 75
   - Set cache prefix rules for conversational sessions (keep last-2-turns cached)
   - Enable telemetry sampling at token-level for first 48 hours

4) Canary script (play-by-play for a canary deploy)
   - Step 0: baseline capture (48h traffic trace) -> save to S3/drive (link to INF-2214)
   - Step 1: deploy variant to 0.5% traffic -> run 1h smoke tests (latency, token-rate, 5 golden prompts)
   - Step 2: increase to 5% for 2h -> monitor cost spike, tail latency, error rate, KV miss rate
   - Abort rules: tail latency increase > 20% vs baseline OR error rate > 0.5% OR quality metric drop exceeds threshold
   - Rollback quick command: call /deploy/rollback <canary-id> (ops playbook)

5) Fast fallback scripts (copy/paste lines for field use)
   - API routing override (for immediate mitigation): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routing/override -d '{"route":"variant-small","duration_mins":30}'
   - Toggle KV-caching aggressive mode: console -> Profiles -> Cache -> Aggressive (ops role required)
   - Emergency cutover: set max_concurrency=1 for heavy requests, route rest to queued-batch endpoint

6) Talking points vs common objections (short bullets)
   - 'We need sub-200ms' -> Ask: what percentile? p50 vs p95. Offer demo using regional dedicated pool + batching knobs; show historical p50 data for similar workloads.
   - 'We can't tolerate quality loss from smaller models' -> Offer fallback only for degraded infra — explain canary A/B with human-in-the-loop for first week. Show evaluation harness to compare outputs (link to eval dashboard).
   - 'Cost unpredictability in burst' -> Explain autoscale+burst buckets and reserved capacity options; provide quick ROI calc example (attach spreadsheet during pilot).

7) Quick decision matrix (one-slide)
   - Rows: problem (latency spike, model regression, infra outage)  Columns: immediate mitigation, medium-term fix, owner (SE/ops/eng)
   - Example cell: latency spike -> immediate mitigation: route to smaller variant (+ telemetry alert) -> medium-term: increase reserved pool or add region -> owner: ops + platform-eng

8) Customer-facing artifacts to hand off after pilot (deliverables list)
   - Pilot runbook (finalized): includes routing policy JSON, canary logs, eval results
   - 2-week run metrics snapshot (tokens, p95 latency, cost/unit)
   - Suggested next steps: reserved capacity quote, long-term rollouts, SLO embedding into SLAs

Practical notes / internal TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Need a concise one-slide diagram exported from the runtime team (ask @Samir; related GH PR linked above).
- Add real curl examples that use the new routing API tokens (security review queued: JIRA INF-2297).
- Validate 'Abort rules' thresholds with SRE (meeting scheduled 2024-11-06).
- Create a small spreadsheet template for SEs to run quick cost comparisons during calls (Riya to own).

Conversation scripts (copyable)
- SE opener (30s): "We've seen this pattern — apps are fast until a tail event; our platform routes to compatible variants automatically and gives you a one-click rollback if quality dips. We'll set conservative canaries for your first week so we can tune thresholds together."
- Ops escalation (60s): "We're seeing a p95 increase from 420ms to 620ms over the last 15 minutes with KV miss rate up 3x. Recommend: set routing override to variant-small and hold current traffic for 10 minutes while we evaluate model trace. If errors remain, initiate canary rollback."

Risks and guardrails to emphasize to customers:
- Fallbacks intentionally may change output distribution. Always record telemetry + eval prompts to detect silent regressions.
- Legal/regulatory: for private deployments confirm KMS/HSM gating before any log export.

Feedback requested (for this draft):
- Simpler abort rule language? (SEs prefer short binary signals.)
- Are the fast-fallback curl examples safe to ship or do they require token-redaction?
- Anything missing in 'deliverables after pilot' that customers expect (legal, procurement checklist, billing contact)?

Notes to self: keep this microdeck under 6 slides. It should be printable as a single-page cheat sheet for SEs to keep in their laptop sleeve.

References and useful links:
- Pilot telemetry dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/pilot/INF-2214/overview
- Routing API spec (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=84533211
- Runbook template (drive): /shared_drives/go-to-market/templates/pilot-runbook-template-v1.docx
- Jira: INF-2214 (pilot telemetry), INF-2297 (routing API security review)

Version history (short):
- 2024-09-12 initial sketch
- 2024-10-02 added canary script and checklist
- 2024-11-04 incorporated ops rollback language and added abort rules (WIP)
